title: Ferroelectric ZnMgO shadow tier lets idle arrays stop refreshing
idea: Inverts 'DRAM must be refreshed while idle.' Pair each DRAM tier with a wurtzite ZnMgO ferroelectric twin tier on the same vertical bitline; when a bank idles, rows copy into the FE tier in parallel and refresh shuts off, restoring on wake, so FE endurance is spent only at idle transitions.
why: Fact 3: idle refresh power (16-33% of idle) falls to near zero without Hf-based HZO.

title: Witness cells per row enable decay-aware differential sensing
idea: Po: the bit knows how old it is. Store each row as differential 2T2C pairs inside the same vertical pillar so both halves leak almost equally (common mode), plus two witness cells written with known 1 and 0 at the same moment; at read the sense threshold is set from the witnesses, so data stays readable after 90% of the charge has leaked.
why: Refresh: retention becomes limited by leakage mismatch, not absolute leakage, ~10-30x longer (seconds), beyond activation and KV lifetimes.

title: Plane-wide charge-pumping refresh restores millions of cells per pulse
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action: instead of read-and-rewrite refresh, apply a periodic gate/source pulse pair to an entire 3D wordline plane. Impact ionization adds holes only in bodies already above a threshold potential (the 1s) while 0s recombine slightly, so every cell on the plane is restored at once without being read.
why: Fact 3: refresh energy and bandwidth fall ~100x because ~10^6 capacitorless cells refresh per pulse with no sense-amp cycles.

title: Canal-lock water-saving basins for bitline precharge
idea: German canal locks store emptied water in side basins at intermediate heights and reuse it to refill; give each mat 8 on-pitch reservoir capacitors at VDD/8 steps so bitlines discharging after a row closes dump charge stepwise into the basins and the next subarray's bitlines refill from them, taking only the final step from the supply.
why: Bitline CV2 (facts 8, 10): stepwise charging with N basins cuts supply energy roughly N-fold; claims ~6-8x lower bitline energy per access.

title: One-run van der Waals superlattice: 100 monolayer channels, 100 tiers
idea: Treat the crystal lattice as the tier stack: grow 100 alternating MoS2/hBN monolayer pairs by wafer-scale MOCVD in one run, with a tier pitch of ~1.5 nm instead of ~60 nm. Then cut vertical slots and contact each monolayer edge as a lateral access-transistor channel; the whole 100-tier stack is ~150 nm tall.
why: The high-AR etch through 26+ tiers is a 3D blocker (fact 2); 40x thinner tiers make 100 tiers etchable at AR <10.

title: Cu2O/ZnO all-oxide CMOS periphery tier above the array
idea: Inverts 'sense amps and decoders must be silicon CMOS under the array.' Build complementary oxide transistors (p-type Cu2O, n-type ZnO:Al) in a BEOL tier over the cell field to hold local sense amps and decoders, freeing the silicon below for more array.
why: Fact 7: moves part of the ~49% periphery off the silicon footprint using abundant Cu, Zn, O and Al.

title: Tin monoxide p-type transistors put sense amps above the array
idea: Pair p-type SnO (Sn2+, sputter/ALD at ~250 C) with n-type ZTO to build complementary oxide sense amplifiers, sub-wordline drivers and local decoders in a BEOL tier directly over each 3D-DRAM mat, so periphery tiles the mat footprint rather than flanking it.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die (fact 7); stacking local periphery over the mat with low-temperature CMOS gives ~30-40% die shrink with no second wafer or hybrid bond, and no indium.

title: Child watching dew form only on grass: area-selective ALD self-alignment
idea: Dew forms on grass, not on rock. Block the oxide with a self-assembled monolayer inhibitor so ALD Ru grows only on exposed metal. Capacitor bottom electrodes and landing pads then self-align to the contacts beneath, with no litho or overlay step.
why: Removes 1-2 critical masks and overlay-limited steps per tier (Fact 4). It needs just one ALD tool and a vapor-prime oven.

title: Retention-graded tiers where data expires before it decays
idea: Po: memory that forgets on purpose. Build a 3D stack whose tiers are designed for graded, guaranteed retention (e.g., 50 ms, 2 s, 60 s via channel material and capacitor size), expose each tier's expiry in the address map, and have the allocator tag every buffer with a lifetime so activations, KV pages and gradients land in a tier that outlives them; refresh circuitry is omitted.
why: Refresh (fact 3): removes the ~46 fJ/bit refresh, 16-33% of idle power and 10-20% bandwidth loss, plus refresh logic area.

title: See-through substrate: backside flood exposure self-aligns every tier
idea: IFR: 'every tier aligns perfectly with no extra masks.' Backward: because glass is transparent, pattern the opaque wordline grid once, then expose each later tier's photoresist with UV flood light from the back of the panel, using the buried metal as an automatic mask so every tier's features self-align with zero overlay error.
why: Litho capital (fact 4) and 3D overlay: masks per tier fall toward zero and the overlay budget vanishes, allowing tighter pitches on cheap panel steppers.

title: IBM racetrack made buildable: horizontal tracks from blanket stacked films
idea: IBM's racetrack memory died because its vertical U-shaped nanowires could not be built and domain walls pinned at etched edges. Deposit magnetic multilayer tracks as blanket films in a 3D-NAND-like layer stack, cut them with one vertical slit etch so each tier becomes a horizontal track, and put write and MTJ read heads on a vertical pillar. Short 16-domain tracks keep shifts under ~20 ns.
why: Density without a transistor per bit (fact 4), with mask count independent of tier count (fact 2). Targets ~16 bits per pillar per tier.

title: Braille embosser's dual-relief stamp: one-imprint wordline and contact
idea: A blind reader's world is embossed, not projected. Pattern the perfectly periodic array with nanoimprint lithography from a master carrying two relief heights, so wordline trench and contact depth are defined in one dual-damascene imprint.
why: Per-layer patterning cost falls to ~1/3-1/5 of EUV, and two litho steps merge into one (Fact 4). The master can be repaired because the array has no randomness.

title: Eliminate photoresist: area-selective deposition self-aligned to lower tiers
idea: Use vapour-delivered inhibitor molecules that adsorb only on dielectric (or only on metal) so the next film grows only where the underlying tier's pattern allows, eliminating resist coat, aqueous TMAH develop and wet strip for self-aligned layers.
why: Water: each resist cycle carries develop, rinse and strip water; making contacts, caps and landing layers self-aligned removes most of them and also removes overlay error.

title: Directed self-assembly patterning made viable by defect-tolerant repairable arrays
idea: Directed self-assembly (DSA) of block copolymers was dropped from DRAM roadmaps because its defect rates were too high. Use DSA to pattern 4F2 pillar arrays without EUV, and tolerate defect densities around 1e-4 through string sparing and defect maps updated in the field.
why: Cuts perhaps 2-3 of the 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4; depreciation is ~55% of wafer cost), with repairability absorbing DSA's defect rate.

title: Child's two-sided paper: memory arrays on both wafer faces
idea: A child asks why we only draw on one side of the page. Build the cell array on the front over the periphery, bond to a carrier, thin to ~5 um, then build a second array on the backside, wired to the same sense amps and decoders through nano-TSVs (as in backside power delivery).
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die; two arrays sharing one periphery layer gives ~1.6-2x bits per mm2 with no extra litho shrink.

title: Potassium hydroxide on (110) silicon etches crystal-perfect vertical cell walls
idea: Align lines along <112> on (110) Si and etch in KOH so the slow {111} planes form atomically smooth vertical walls 20-40 nm thick at >100:1 aspect ratio; a deposited oxide/TiN wordline stack crossing the walls turns each wall into a vertical string of DRAM cells.
why: Single-crystal vertical semiconductor sheets for stacked cells (fact 2) without DRIE or EUV (fact 4), from a heated beaker; smooth walls trim the interface-trap leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Inductive-coil links replace TSVs between stacked dies
idea: Scale the transformer down: draw ~20-um on-chip coils in thick 180-nm-era metal on each thinned die and pass data magnetically through the stack at Gb/s per coil, so stacked DRAM needs no TSV etch, fill or keep-out zones.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): removes TSV area and yield loss, using old tools.

title: Darkroom development: pillar-foot gain transistor reads a 0.5 fF cell
idea: Like a latent photographic image amplified by development, store only ~0.5 fF per 3D cell and put one thin-film gain transistor at the foot of every 16-cell vertical local bitline; the cell perturbs only ~1 fF of local line and the gain device converts it into current on a 100 mV-swing global line.
why: Energy per access and capacitor wall (facts 1, 8, 10): switched capacitance per read falls from ~85 fF at 1 V to a few fF plus a low-swing global line; claims ~10x lower read energy.

title: Eliminate periphery from the memory wafer: subarray-granular hybrid bonding
idea: The memory wafer carries only cell arrays with 16:1 bitline muxes at each subarray edge; sense amps, decoders and I/O sit on a separately made logic wafer joined by ~400 nm pitch hybrid bonds at subarray granularity.
why: Periphery ~49%: array efficiency rises toward ~85-90%, and periphery moves to a cheaper or better-suited logic node; ~1.6x bits per memory wafer.

title: Array tiers on reclaimed or glass carriers, bonded to foundry periphery
idea: [Box: IGZO 1T1C/2T0C tiers | IGZO | standard SA | CMOS-bonded-array hybrid bond | reclaimed Si or glass carrier | DUV-only; periphery from U.S. 22-28 nm foundries] BEOL IGZO array tiers do not need single-crystal Si, so build them on cheap reclaimed or glass carrier wafers and hybrid-bond them to periphery wafers bought from existing U.S. 22-28 nm DUV foundries.
why: Scarce resources (prime CZ wafers depend on Spruce Pine quartz crucibles) and U.S. manufacturability: about half the prime-wafer demand per bit, and no EUV on either wafer.

title: Recess only passing-wordline segments with one mask
idea: Rearrange the buried wordline: one added mask exposes only the segments where wordlines cross isolation (the passing gates) and recesses them deeper, moving their field away from the neighboring cell's storage junction while active-crossing segments stay at normal depth.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): passing-gate coupling drives the ~1k-activation threshold; a deeper passing segment could raise it several-fold with zero cell-area cost.

title: One hybrid-bond pad per mat: a million vertical channels, no TSVs
idea: Jump from 1024 TSVs per HBM die to ~10^6 hybrid-bond pads at 1-um pitch, giving every DRAM mat its own vertical channel into the compute die directly below. There is no TSV keep-out and no SerDes, and wires are ~10 um long.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6) and data-movement energy (fact 5): ~0.05-0.2 pJ/bit, and HBM's ~3x wafer area per bit is recovered.

title: Retune idle 3D NAND lines into quasi-volatile charge-trap DRAM
idea: Substitute NAND's ~5 nm FN-programmed tunnel oxide with a ~1.5-2 nm direct-tunneling oxide in a 3D NOR-organized charge-trap stack: writes in ~10-50 ns at <4 V, retention seconds-hours (refreshed), low-field tunneling for very high endurance, on existing 200+ layer NAND tools with mask changes only.
why: Capital and supply (fact 4): converts underused 3D-stacking capex into DRAM-class capacity with ~5-10x fewer refreshes and NAND-like cost per bit.

title: One via mask personalizes page, bank and 2T2C mode
idea: Business model reversal: fabricate a single universal DRAM wafer and make products with one via mask that rewires mats into 1 kB or 2 kB pages, HBM pseudo-channels, or a 2T2C mode (two cells per bit for double signal and ~10x retention, half density) for automotive and low-refresh customers.
why: Capital (fact 4) and supply flexibility: one wafer flow serves many SKUs; capacity shifts between markets within weeks; the 2T2C SKU attacks refresh (fact 3).

title: Self-aligned dual-workfunction gate tames storage-side GIDL in lateral 3D cells
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: in each lateral 3D access transistor, recess the gate metal laterally from the storage-hole side and refill that ~5 nm edge with a low-workfunction metal, keeping a high-workfunction gate on the bitline side for drive. Field at the storage junction drops and the leakage tail shrinks, with no new mask because the storage hole itself defines the recess.
why: Fact 3: ~10x lower tail leakage -> ~4-8x longer refresh interval, recovering most of the 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth spent on refresh.

title: Grating-maker method: solid-state deep-UV interference lithography for arrays
idea: Makers of astronomical diffraction gratings print meter-scale periodic lines by interfering laser beams, with no mask; use a frequency-quintupled Nd:YAG (213 nm) or solid-state 193 nm laser, built on nonlinear crystals with no argon-fluoride or neon gas, in two-beam and four-beam interference to print the array's line and hole lattices at ~40 nm pitch. Spacer pitch-splitting then reaches ~20 nm.
why: EUV/ArF dependence and their He/Ne/Kr/Ar gases removed (fact 4); interference tool ~$5-10M vs $200M, ~5x lower array patterning cost per layer.

title: Vertical bitlines climb bonded array tiers to one shared sense amp
idea: [Box: 1T1C charge | buried-channel Si FET | sense amp multiplexed across tiers | 8-tier stack of array-only wafers | thinned Si | hybrid bond + sub-um through-tier vias] Stack 4-8 thinned array-only wafers (no periphery) on one periphery wafer and drop every bitline segment through through-tier vias to a sense amp time-shared among tiers, so sense amps and decoders are amortized over 8x the cells.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): periphery share falls toward ~10%, ~1.6-1.8x bits per processed silicon area, and HBM-class capacity without per-die TSV keep-outs (fact 6).

title: One wordline plate gates two channel tiers: shared double-gate stack
idea: Worse: give every channel tier its own wordline tier and isolation, so each bit costs ~3 films of stack height. Flip: build repeating channel/gate/channel/isolation units where each metal wordline plate gates the channel above and the channel below, with upper and lower channels routed to alternate vertical bitlines so the two cells stay independently addressable.
why: Stack height per bit falls ~35%, so ~1.5x more tiers fit the same etch: a 100-tier-depth etch holds ~150 effective tiers, enough for ~10x at unchanged etch and similar deposition cost.

title: Bubble-memory boot-loop map lets 3D tiers ship with dead strings
idea: Bubble chips shipped with several percent of minor loops defective plus a boot loop telling the controller which to skip; do the same in 3D DRAM: each mat stores a triple-replicated map of bitline segments whose cells fail, and column logic skips them at full speed. Up to 1% failing cells per mat are masked at test and remapped in the field.
why: Facts 2 and 4: tolerating 1% bad cells lets low-quality poly/oxide channels and 100+ tiers yield, cutting capital per good bit and the 3D break-even tier count.

title: Nanomechanical gap switch isolates the gain-cell storage gate
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution, used in reverse (field -> mechanics): replace the write transistor of a 2T0C gain cell with an electrostatically actuated vertical NEMS contact switch built in the tier stack. An open air gap has essentially zero leakage, so the read transistor's gate keeps its charge until gate-dielectric leakage alone drains it.
why: Fact 3: refresh interval from ~64 ms to minutes; ~10 ns mechanical write; requires contact endurance near 10^15 (graphene or Ru contacts), which is the main risk.

title: Folded U-cell stacks transistor over capacitor inside one tier
idea: Worse: lay the access transistor and capacitor end to end so lateral 3D cells run ~2x longer than the bitline pitch needs. Flip: build each tier as two sublayers where the channel runs out from the bitline in the upper sublayer, turns down through a self-aligned via at the far end, and the capacitor runs back underneath toward the bitline.
why: Halves lateral cell length for ~1.5x taller tiers, ~1.4x net density per etch depth, so 10x needs ~30% fewer tier-depth microns at the same cost (facts 1, 2).

title: Bubble-memory major/minor loop organization for stacked skyrmion tiers
idea: Reuse the bubble chip's architecture: in each tier of a sputtered magnetic multilayer stack, skyrmions circulate in hundreds of parallel minor loops driven by spin-orbit current, and a block-transfer gate swaps a whole page into one major loop read by a single MTJ. One etch defines the loops through all tiers, so tiers are added by deposition, not masks.
why: Facts 4 and 7: one reader per ~1e5 bits collapses periphery and extra tiers cost deposition only; a dense second-tier working memory at ~100 ns page access.

title: Voltage-stacked tiers reuse one supply current through four arrays
idea: Power four tier groups in series (0-1 V, 1-2 V, 2-3 V, 3-4 V) so the same current flows through each array once, with interleaved address mapping to balance activity, small push-pull regulators to absorb mismatch and level shifters at tier boundaries.
why: I^2R and conversion losses scale with current: delivering 4 V at a quarter of the current cuts PDN loss ~16x and needs ~4x fewer power TSVs and bumps, attacking the HBM TSV tax (fact 6) and power-delivery overhead.

title: Two-mask-per-tier self-aligned crosspoint gain cell for $1 IoT
idea: A $1 IoT chip cannot afford 30 masks, so define every memory tier with exactly two orthogonal line masks, as in crosspoint memory: line set A forms the write wordline plus storage gate, line set B forms the bitline plus vertical channel, and a 2T gain cell self-aligns at every crossing. All tiers reuse the same two masks.
why: Mask count and capital (fact 4): 2 masks per tier instead of 5-7 EUV layers, 4F2 per crossing, ~2-3x lower cost per bit at mature nodes, and memory buildable in the BEOL over a cheap MCU.

title: Spider-silk fiber drawing shrinks a coax-capacitor preform to nanoscale
idea: As spiders and tendons build hierarchy by drawing and bundling fibres, draw a glass preform containing metal-insulator-metal coaxial rods down ~1000x, bundle and redraw (as for photonic-crystal fibre) to ~50 nm coax pitch, then slice perpendicular into 1-2 um wafers that are dense coax-capacitor arrays to bond onto access-transistor wafers.
why: Capacitor charge wall and EUV: capacitors of any length/AR made with no etch or lithography, Cs set by slice thickness; bit cost falls if fibre-draw throughput scales.

title: Dielectrophoretic placement of single-crystal nanowires as tier access transistors
idea: Dielectrophoresis: single-crystal Si nanowires are grown off-wafer, suspended in fluid, and pulled by an AC field into electrode gaps in every BEOL tier. Each tier gets crystalline lateral access transistors at <400 C without per-tier epitaxy.
why: Solves the missing lateral transistor in 3D DRAM (fact 2); claim crystalline mobility and low leakage in every tier with a cheap, low-temperature process.

title: Spatial-ALD carousel deposits ten tiers per wafer pass
idea: Worse: deposit 200 tiers sequentially in chamber-based ALD/CVD so deposition time becomes the new cost wall. Flip: run wafers through rotary spatial-ALD carousels with gas-separated precursor zones that lay down alternating channel/dielectric/sacrificial films at ~10x the throughput per tool, with in-line ellipsometry closing the loop on each tier's thickness.
why: Keeps per-tier deposition at ~0.1-0.2% of wafer cost, so the ~150-200 tiers needed for 10x density add <30% to cost and less capex than chamber tools (fact 4).

title: Shingled-recording discipline: overlapping cells written in sequential bands
idea: Adapted from SMR hard drives, which overlap tracks and require sequential zone writes: adjacent storage nodes along a row share partially overlapping electrodes with no isolation, and a band is written in order so each write fixes the trailing cell's charge; reads remain random.
why: Removing isolation spacing gives ~2-3F2 cells, ~2-3x density (fact 4); stacked in tiers this is a 100x path for read-mostly AI weights and KV cache; trade-off: band-granular writes.

title: Carbon-nanotube forests as capacitor bottom electrodes on each pad
idea: [Box: MIM charge on CNT bundle | Si VCT | charge-share SA | BEOL | Si | self-aligned catalyst dot + ~450 C CVD + conformal ALD ZrO2/TiN] Grow a short vertically aligned CNT bundle from a catalyst dot plated selectively on each storage-node pad, then coat it conformally with high-k and a TiN plate; the forest gives 10-30x surface area per footprint at 1-2 um height with no mold etch.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): surface area replaces the aspect-ratio race and skips the 60-75:1 oxide mold etch.

title: Eliminate the distinct periphery process: array-transistor-only periphery
idea: Build sense amps, decoders and drivers from the same vertical channel devices as the array, in a single homogeneous device process, accepting larger periphery circuits that are tucked under the array.
why: Water: the planar periphery CMOS flow (many wells, implants, gate stacks, salicide cleans) is ~40% of mask and wet steps; removing it and stacking tiers gives ~10x less water per bit.

title: Venetian blinds: slanted overlapping plate capacitors cut by angled ion beam
idea: Blind slats overlap one another: angled ion-beam etching at 45-60 degrees cuts slanted trenches so each cell's plate capacitor leans over its neighbors' footprint like overlapping slats. Plate area reaches 3-4x the cell footprint with only a ~20:1 vertical etch.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): ~5 fF at ~3x lower vertical aspect ratio, so pillar toppling and etch-tool limits relax.

title: Baker's dozen tier: build N+1 legacy dies, cull the weakest
idea: Bakers add a thirteenth roll against shortfalls; stack 9 mature DRAM dies for an 8-high product and route them through a small switch matrix in the base die so the worst tier, by retention or row-hammer threshold, is disabled after assembly test.
why: Converts stack failures into a ~12% silicon spare and lets marginal binned-out mature dies ship, lifting usable stack supply ~15-25% (facts 6, 9).

title: Lottery drum: tier-randomized row placement re-keyed every refresh window
idea: A lottery drum reshuffles before every draw: in a 3D or stacked DRAM, a keyed permutation maps logically consecutive rows to physically non-adjacent rows in different tiers, and the key rotates every 32 ms window as refresh migrates rows through a small spare region. A hammer pattern cannot keep hitting the same physical neighbors, and the DDR5/HBM command set and timing are untouched.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): targeted multi-sided attacks lose physical adjacency; effective threshold up 10-100x with no controller change.

title: Backside capacitor on a 4F2 vertical-channel cell
idea: Worse: cram capacitor, bitline and wordline onto the same face so they fight over one 4F2 footprint. Flip: build vertical-channel transistors with buried bitlines and the periphery on the front, flip-bond to a carrier, thin from the back, and form the capacitors on the exposed channel bottoms so each capacitor gets the full footprint with no bitline contacts threading between them.
why: Enables true 4F2 (1.5x over 6F2, fact 4) without bitline-capacitor contact conflicts, and decouples the capacitor thermal budget from the transistor.

title: Child's rubber stamp: micro-transfer printing memory dielets onto logic
idea: A child stamps hundreds of stickers at once. Release 50x50 um memory dielets from their source wafer on undercut tethers, then pick thousands at a time with a PDMS stamp and print them onto a logic wafer at +/-1.5 um placement.
why: Memory from any small fab can be printed millimetres from compute with no interposer or TSVs (Facts 5, 6). A uTP tool costs ~$1-2M.

title: Stacked SIMOX: multi-energy oxygen implants build tiered crystalline silicon
idea: Use ion range as a depth ruler: implant oxygen at two to four energies with 1990s high-current implanters and anneal, forming multiple buried oxide layers and so several single-crystal silicon tiers inside one bulk wafer with no epitaxy or bonding. Each tier hosts lateral access transistors.
why: 3D DRAM lacks crystalline upper tiers (fact 2): low-leakage single-crystal channels in 3-4 tiers at low cost; the honest catch is the limited tier count.

title: Bunk beds: upper cell tier serves as lower tier's sensing reference
idea: Bunk beds stack two sleepers on one floor plan: layer-transfer a second single-crystal cell tier above the first array's capacitors and drop its bitlines to the same sense amps, so each sense amp compares a lower-tier bitline with the upper-tier bitline directly overhead (vertical folded pairing). Sense amps and periphery are shared, and the part is a standard DDR5/HBM die of twice the capacity.
why: Periphery (fact 7) and density: periphery per bit halves (~49% to ~33% of die area), ~1.7x bits/mm2, with folded-bitline noise immunity at open-bitline density.

title: Voltage-stacked tiers recycle bitline charge in series
idea: Limit: supply current cut 8x. Run eight tier groups in series between 8 V and 0 V, each swinging only its own 1 V slice. Charge dumped by one tier's bitline precharge becomes the supply of the tier below.
why: Fact 10: breaks the CV2 voltage floor at system level; up to about 2-4x lower array energy and 8x less power-delivery current and bump count.

title: Defect charge-state memory in stacked silicon-carbide sheets
idea: Po: the memory cell is a single missing atom. Store bits as the charge state of implanted point defects (e.g., divacancies in 4H-SiC) arrayed in thin bonded SiC sheets; a gate pulse moves the local Fermi level to set the charge state, which persists for days at room temperature because the level sits ~1 eV deep in the gap.
why: Zero refresh with wear-free switching (no atoms move); sensing through a nearby channel's conductance. Speed and density are speculative.

title: Stack-of-stacks: hybrid-bonded sixteen-tier superlattice modules
idea: Limit: strain allows no more than 20 Si/SiGe pairs per epi run. Grow strain-safe 16-tier modules on separate wafers, process their lateral cells, then hybrid-bond eight modules face-to-face and back-to-back with vertical bitline vias crossing each bond.
why: Fact 2: reaches 128 tiers without epi relaxation defects, and module yield is binned before stacking.

title: Wire-bonder pin forest: bond-via arrays link legacy dies to logic
idea: Use installed wire bonders as 3D printers to stand dense forests of vertical 25 um copper wires on a logic die, mold and grind them flat, and face-down-bond mature DRAM dies on top as an HBM-like wide bus with no TSV process.
why: Sidesteps the HBM TSV tax (fact 6) entirely in existing OSAT lines (~10-20k wires per stack) and places memory adjacent to compute to cut I/O energy toward ~2 pJ/bit (fact 5).

title: Sodium beta-alumina double-layer nanocapacitors in flat 3D tiers
idea: Inverts 'cell capacitance comes from a dielectric's permittivity.' Sandwich a 2-3 nm Na-beta-alumina solid electrolyte between TiN electrodes so the electric double layer gives ~20-40 uF/cm², 3-6x a high-k film, allowing flat lateral capacitors in each tier.
why: Facts 1-2: flat capacitors remove the 3D capacitor blocker using Na, Al, O, Ti, N only; ns ion response and self-discharge are the open questions.

title: Solid-electrolyte double-layer nanocapacitors as DRAM storage nodes
idea: [Box: electric-double-layer ionic charge | Si VCT | charge-share SA | BEOL over array | Si | ALD solid proton/Li-ion conductor between blocking electrodes] Replace the dielectric with an ultrathin solid electrolyte so charge sits in Helmholtz double layers (~20 uF/cm2, roughly 3x a 0.5 nm-EOT high-k), giving ~5 fF with only ~10:1 aspect ratio.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): ~3x capacitance per area, cutting capacitor AR ~6x; risks are ionic response time (<100 ns needed) and electronic leakage.

title: Memory tier slipped into Intel 18A backside-power stack
idea: Fuse logic backside power delivery with memory: after the US PowerVia flow thins the wafer, deposit a low-temperature capacitor plus thin-film-transistor memory tier on the backside between the transistors and backside power rails, giving each logic die tens to hundreds of MB of DRAM-class memory microns from its cores.
why: Data movement (fact 5): <0.1 pJ/bit vertical access; absorbs cache/KV traffic so accelerators need fewer HBM bits; built in existing US leading-edge fabs.

title: Self-organized anodic TiO2 nanotubes as both dielectric and 3D mold
idea: [Box: rutile TiO2 charge (k~80-100) | VCT | charge-share SA | BEOL | Si | Ti anodization + RuO2-templated rutile anneal] Anodize a sputtered Ti film over the landing pads into vertically aligned nanotubes nucleated on each pad, crystallize them to rutile on a RuO2 seed, and fill tube cores with the storage electrode, so the high-k dielectric grows itself in 3D with no hole lithography or plasma etch.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1, k~70 target) and no EUV (fact 4): mold, etch and dielectric deposition collapse into one electrochemical step.

title: Registration-free anodic alumina capacitor forest at room temperature
idea: Under 400 C, anodize a sputtered 3 um Al film over the transistor tier at room temperature to self-form 25 nm pores (AR over 100) with no litho or plasma etch. Each storage-node pad is wider than the pore pitch, so it captures 2-3 pores. ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN at 300 C lines the pores.
why: Facts 1 and 4: AR over 100 without a high-AR etch tool; Cs above 6 fF with no capacitor mask.

title: Blu-ray layer focus: threshold-window gates select tiers by voltage
idea: Borrowed from multilayer optical discs where focus depth picks the layer: each tier's access transistor has two series gates on two shared vertical lines, with thresholds graded up the stack on one and down on the other, so voltage level k on both turns on only tier k, with no per-tier staircase contact.
why: Removes staircase contacts and per-tier drivers for ~8 tiers per gate pair (facts 2,7); staircase area ~-80%.

title: Eliminate wafers and wet benches: roll-to-roll vacuum web tiers
idea: Deposit oxide-semiconductor capacitor-transistor tiers on a moving stainless or polyimide web inside a vacuum roll coater, patterning with in-line laser ablation and shadow-roll masks, then laminate cut sheets into stacks.
why: Water and capital: vacuum web coating uses almost no process water and costs tens of millions per line; it suits slower, higher-capacity working-memory tiers.

title: Eliminate the page: AND-gated two-transistor pillar cells
idea: In a vertical-bitline 3D array, each cell has two series access gates, a tier wordline and a pillar-select gate, so a cell connects only when both are high; one activation opens a single 64-tier pillar instead of an 8 Kb row.
why: 128x overfetch: activation energy per useful bit falls ~10-50x and row hammer shrinks because no full row is opened; the stack absorbs the second transistor's area.

title: Delay-line recirculation with decode-and-correct at every string lap
idea: Mercury delay lines regenerated every pulse on each lap; revive that in shift-register 3D strings: as data pass the string-foot regenerator, a short BCH codeword is decoded and rewritten corrected every lap (~1 us), so per-transfer and leakage errors of up to 1% per cell never accumulate.
why: Facts 2 and 3: allows leaky, trap-rich channels and 128+ tier strings, while refresh becomes free scrubbing; near-NAND density for working memory.

title: Oxygen: porous-silicon oxidation carves many SOI tiers from one epi stack
idea: Grow an epi stack alternating p+ (~1e19) and lightly doped Si, open slits, anodize in HF so only the p+ layers become mesoporous, then oxidize them at ~850 C into buried oxide (FIPOS); the lightly doped layers remain single-crystal device tiers.
why: Crystalline multi-tier SOI with no germanium (no SiGe mismatch limit on tier count) and no bonding cycles; attacks the lateral-transistor blocker (fact 2) at epi-reactor cost.

title: Epitaxial vertical pnpn thyristor pillars as capacitorless 4F2 cells
idea: [Box: thyristor bistable conduction | gated self-latching pnpn | current sense | monolithic, repeatable by layer transfer | Si | in-situ doped blanket epitaxy then pillar etch] Grow a blanket p+/n/p/n+ epitaxial stack so junction positions are set by deposition, etch it into pillars and wrap a gate on the p-base; the latched/blocking state is dynamic storage with large read current and no capacitor.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) and 3D (fact 2): no capacitor, junctions defined by epitaxy not lithography, and identical stacks can be transferred tier by tier.

title: Nacre-tablet segmented tiers let 3D stacks pass 200 layers
idea: Like nacre's staggered aragonite tablets glued by thin biopolymer, break each deposited tier into ~50 um tablets separated by narrow stress-relief trenches filled with low-modulus porous SiOC, staggering trench positions tier to tier so cracks deflect and film stress cannot accumulate into wafer bow.
why: 3D layer-count limit from wafer bow and cracking: could allow 2-3x more tiers before warpage blocks lithography and bonding.

title: Vertical charge-coupled columns replace per-bit access transistors
idea: Substitute the per-cell access transistor with CCD-style transfer gates: each 4F² footprint hosts a vertical column of 16-32 potential wells (one per tier, formed by tier gate-planes wrapped around a shared single-crystal Si pillar), and a 3-phase clock shifts the column's charge packets up to one sense node at the top and writes them back down. Only that top node needs a transistor and contact.
why: Attacks fact 2 (lateral transistor blocks 3D DRAM) and per-tier contact count: N bits per 4F² with 1/N the transistors, ~8-10x bits/footprint at 32 tiers; column access ~20-40 ns suits page/stream tiers.

title: Automotive tier-RAID: erasure code striped across stacked array tiers
idea: Automotive ASIL-D allows no silent bit loss at 150 C; stripe each 64-byte line across 9 tiers of a 3D array (8 data + 1 parity) read in parallel, so any single tier with weak or hammered cells is rebuilt on the fly. Refresh can then be set by the typical tier rather than the worst cell anywhere in the stack.
why: The leakage tail sets refresh (fact 3): ~4x longer refresh interval because single-tier tail failures are corrected; tier yield (fact 2) improves at ~12% parity overhead.

title: Clamped-bitline charge-transfer sensing makes bitline capacitance irrelevant
idea: TRIZ #12 Equipotentiality: hold each long bitline at a constant potential with a local cascode transistor so the bitline never swings; the cell's charge flows through the cascode into a ~0.5 fF sense node. Signal then scales with Qcell/Csense rather than Qcell/Cbitline.
why: Fact 1 and 7: ~4x more cells per sense amp (less periphery) or ~half the cell capacitance at equal margin; bitline CV2 energy ~5x lower.

title: Hot-spare tiers from 30-year industrial controllers raise stack yield
idea: An industrial controller must run 30 years unserviced, so each 3D array carries two spare tiers and a per-mat tier-remap table in the bonded logic layer; a failing tier is retired in the field and its data copied to a spare. In the fab the same mechanism lets a 64-tier stack ship with any two bad tiers.
why: Tier-count yield blocks 3D DRAM (fact 2): 0.99^64 = 53% compound tier yield rises to ~97% with two spares, ~1.5x lower cost per bit.

title: Eliminate the wafer fab entirely: thermally drawn fiber DRAM
idea: Assemble a macroscopic preform of semiconductor, glass and metal stripes encoding capacitor-transistor cross-sections, thermally draw it into kilometres of fiber with thousands of parallel nanoscale cells, then cut, align and tile fiber segments into planks addressed at their ends.
why: Capital intensity: replaces lithography with fiber-draw towers costing millions instead of billions; density and access speed are open questions.

title: Straintronic nanomagnets switched by a shared piezo wordline film
idea: Magnetostriction: each non-volatile bit is a FeGa or Co nanomagnet sitting on an AlScN piezo film that forms the wordline. A voltage pulse on the film strains the row's magnets past their anisotropy barrier, a bitline bias picks which magnets flip, and an MTJ reads the state. No write current flows.
why: Attacks energy per bit and the voltage floor (fact 10) for non-volatile tiers; claim ~1-10 aJ writes, 100x below STT-MRAM, and stackable BEOL tiers.

title: Face-to-face HBM pairs halve the TSV count
idea: Rearrange HBM from face-to-back stacking to face-to-face pairs: two core dies are hybrid-bonded face-to-face at ~1 um pitch with no TSVs between them, and only pair-to-pair interfaces use TSVs, with one die's TSVs serving both.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): TSV count and keep-out area halve; dense face-to-face bonds let two dies share I/O and repair logic; ~10-15% more bits per wafer and better stack yield.

title: Alveolar bulb capacitors: narrow neck with stacked spherical sacs
idea: Like lung alveoli hiding huge area behind a narrow airway, etch a modest 25:1 hole through alternating doped/undoped Si layers, then use a dopant-selective isotropic etch to inflate spherical sacs at each sensitive layer before ALD electrode/dielectric lining, forming a necklace of alveoli on one neck.
why: Capacitor charge wall: 2-3x electrode area versus a straight pillar of the same AR, giving target Cs with a far easier etch.

title: Magnify die to the full wafer: wafer-scale DRAM
idea: Make a 300 mm wafer one memory, with no dicing: tiles are linked by an on-wafer mesh with spare-tile rerouting. Bond it face-to-face to a wafer-scale compute wafer, so there are no packages, PHYs or scribe lines.
why: Data movement and packaging: about 1 TB per wafer pair at about 0.1 pJ/bit, recovering about 5-8% of wafer area lost to scribe lines and edges.

title: Roll-to-roll oxide-TFT DRAM sheets laminated into thick stacks
idea: Po: memory is sold by the metre like tape. Sputter and nanoimprint oxide-TFT plus capacitor arrays roll-to-roll on 10 um polished metal foil at <300 C, then laminate 50-200 sheets with anisotropic conductive film and laser-drilled vertical bitline vias, the way multilayer ceramic capacitors stack 1000 layers.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4) and U.S. manufacturability: no EUV and no vacuum wafer fab for array layers; low per-layer density (F~100 nm) means it wins $/bit for capacity tiers, not latency.

title: Fifteen-minute city: a private DRAM tile bonded over every core
idea: Urbanists keep essentials within a short walk; hybrid-bond at 1 um pitch a 64 MB 3D DRAM tile directly above each compute-core cluster so its data travels under 100 um vertically through ~10k bonds with 0.3 V signalling, with no PHY, SerDes or interposer.
why: Data movement (fact 5): HBM 3-4 pJ/bit and DDR5 10-20 pJ/bit vs ~0.05-0.1 pJ/bit transport; claims >10x lower energy per delivered bit.

title: Kitchen sponge: gyroid block-copolymer electrode fills each capacitor well
idea: A sponge hides huge internal surface: spin a gyroid-forming block copolymer into each capacitor well, remove one block, and ALD-coat the continuous 3D network with TiN/high-k/TiN so the electrode becomes a triply periodic minimal surface. At a 20-25 nm period the internal area is about 10x that of a plain cylinder.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): 5 fF at AR ~15:1, or 20+ fF at today's aspect ratio for much longer retention.

title: Kirkendall-hollowed double-wall nanotube capacitors in each tier
idea: Kirkendall effect: lateral Ni or Cu nanowires are deposited in each tier and coated with an oxidizing or sulfiding shell, then annealed. Unequal diffusion hollows each wire into a tube, and both the inner and outer walls become electrode surface without any deep etch.
why: Raises Cs at fixed aspect ratio (fact 1) and avoids AR 60-75 etches in 3D tiers (fact 2); claim ~1.8x capacitor area for the same footprint.

title: Rubber stamp: nanoimprint replaces EUV on the periodic array layers
idea: A rubber stamp copies a pattern with no optics: because the cell array is perfectly periodic, pattern the capacitor-hole, bitline and active layers with jet-and-flash nanoimprint (one master, many replica templates), and keep EUV or DUV only for the irregular periphery. The die and its interface match standard DDR5.
why: Litho capital (fact 4): 3-5 of the 5-7 EUV layers move to imprint tools at ~1/5 the cost; claim wafer cost -10-15% and less dependence on the single EUV supplier.

title: Siloxane soft-stamp nanoimprint copies one e-beam master to every tier
idea: Write a single 4F2-pitch Si master by e-beam, cast hard-PDMS/PDMS stamps from it, and UV-nanoimprint the critical cell layer of every tier on every wafer at ~15 nm resolution, using the master only to replicate stamps and a mask aligner for overlay.
why: Capital per critical layer falls ~100x vs EUV (fact 4); imprint has been trialed by NAND makers and imprint tools are common in university fabs.

title: Hemoglobin cooperativity: stacked GaN/AlN tunnel-diode pairs self-latch each bit
idea: Hemoglobin's cooperative binding gives a sharp two-state switch; give each 3D cell a vertically stacked Goto pair of AlN/GaN resonant-tunneling diodes (~2 eV band offset keeps negative resistance at high temperature) on the storage node, so the node is bistable and self-restores against leakage, read through one vertical access transistor.
why: Eliminates refresh at 125 C (tunnel-SRAM at near-DRAM density): refresh's 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth go to near zero, with standby set by RTD valley current.

title: Room-temperature surface-activated bonding of 5 um memory dies
idea: Under 400 C, Ar-beam surface activation bonds Cu/SiO2 die faces at room temperature, so thermal-expansion warpage never builds up. This allows 5 um dies and 32-48-high stacks.
why: Fact 6: about 3x bits per stack height with no thermocompression yield loss.

title: Array-logic-array sandwich: one periphery wafer serves two faces
idea: Inverts 'periphery sits beside or beneath one array.' Hybrid-bond array wafers to both faces of a thinned periphery wafer so each sense amp senses an open bitline above and its reference bitline below, halving periphery per bit and giving a naturally matched reference.
why: Fact 7: the ~49% periphery share can drop to ~25% effective; symmetric above/below bitlines improve noise immunity.

title: Velcro: press-fit nanowire forests make stacked memory dies reworkable
idea: Forced connection to hook-and-loop: grow 2 um Cu nanowire or CNT forests on both die faces at 10 um pad pitch, so dies interlock by room-temperature press-fit with low contact resistance. A die that fails stack test is pulled and replaced before the final anneal and underfill lock the stack.
why: HBM stack yield loss of 20-30% (fact 6) becomes rework: claim stack yield ~70% to ~95% and cost per HBM bit about -20%.

title: Z-RAM reborn: floating-body cells in natively insulated stacked nanosheet tiers
idea: Z-RAM died because floating-body storage needed costly SOI wafers and its hole-storage margin collapsed at scale. Build it in a Si/SiGe superlattice 3D stack where removing the SiGe leaves every Si tier naturally insulated (SOI for free), and bias the wordline plane of the tier below negative as a back-gate that deepens the hole well, so each tier is a capacitorless 1T cell.
why: Removes the capacitor blocker for 3D DRAM (fact 2) and sidesteps the charge wall (fact 1). The back-gate targets about 10x Z-RAM's retention, with 26+ tiers and no capacitor etch.

title: Alpha-In2Se3 ferroelectric-semiconductor channel tiers stacked by the dozen
idea: Interlocked in-plane and out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization: atomically thin α-In2Se3 is both the channel and the ferroelectric. Gate pulses flip its polarization, which non-volatilely shifts channel conduction, and its ~1 nm thickness allows dozens of vdW tiers in vertical strings.
why: Gives a thin non-volatile 3D cell with no capacitor (facts 1 and 2); claim tier pitch <15 nm and 30+ tiers.

title: GPU-owned sense amps: array stack bonded straight onto accelerator
idea: Limit: no base die and no DRAM-process periphery. Array-only layers with 8:1 bitline muxes are hybrid-bonded at fine pitch directly onto the accelerator die. Sense amps, decoders and controllers are built in the accelerator's 3 nm logic, at about 1/4 the area of DRAM-process periphery.
why: Facts 5 and 7: removes the HBM PHY and base die; data movement drops toward 0.3 pJ/bit and array dies become near-100% cells.

title: Vertical CCD columns shift charge through 3D NAND-style gate stacks
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: through a 192-layer deposited (not patterned) gate stack, clock three-phase pulses along a vertical single-crystal channel so charge packets march down the column like a CCD. A base amplifier reads and regenerates every packet on each lap, so refresh is continuous and free.
why: Fact 2 and 4: ~64-192 bits per lithographic hole with no capacitor or per-bit contacts (~10x bits per litho layer); access is serial (~50-100 ns average per 64-position column).

title: Home renovator's second storey: post-CMOS capacitor tier on foundry logic
idea: Like adding a storey to a finished house, buy MPW logic wafers laid out as 1T1C access arrays with exposed top-metal landing pads. In a university cleanroom, add 3 masks: 5 um oxide, holes, then ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN capacitors.
why: Puts eDRAM-class memory on any logic node without the foundry offering it, ~3-4x denser than SRAM. Capex fits a 10-person team (U.S. manufacturability).

title: Plate-pulsed sensing doubles signal so low-k capacitors suffice
idea: Inverts 'the capacitor plate is a static common electrode.' Segment the plate per sub-array row and pulse it during sensing so stored charge is pumped onto the bitline with ~2x signal, letting abundant-element dielectrics (Al2O3/TiO2 laminates, k~30-40) meet sense margin with ~half the Cs.
why: Fact 1 under the constraint: compensates by architecture for losing Hf/Zr/Ru high-k; Cs requirement drops ~2x.

title: Infiltrated block-copolymer dots replace EUV pillar-hole patterning
idea: Substitute EUV contact/pillar patterning with self-assembly: PS-b-P2VP cylinders form a hexagonal lattice at 20-28 nm pitch inside coarse ArF-dry guide trenches, 3 cycles of sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O) turn P2VP domains into AlOx hard-mask dots, PS is O2-ashed and the pattern transferred with Cl2/HBr.
why: Litho capital (fact 4): sub-20 nm dense pillar arrays without EUV; SIS supplies fluorine-free etch selectivity (silicon-containing BCPs would need CF4).

title: Early-2010s 4F2 vertical-channel DRAM fixed with backside metal bitlines
idea: Vertical-pillar 4F2 DRAM was shelved in the early 2010s, largely because buried bitlines of doped silicon had high resistance and floating pillar bodies caused hysteresis. After thinning, form low-resistance Cu or Ru bitlines from the backside that contact the pillar bottoms. Add a thin backside body-tie rail along each pillar row to pin the body potential.
why: Enables 4F2 instead of 6F2 (fact 4), about 33% less area per bit, with no extra EUV layer. Bitline resistance falls ~50x, allowing longer bitlines and fewer sense amps (fact 7).

title: Glassblower's drawn fiber: coaxial capacitors pulled from a preform
idea: The glassblower does not etch holes; they draw them. Assemble a macroscopic preform of low-melting metal cores in glass-dielectric cladding with outer metal, draw it 1000x, bundle and redraw it to ~100 nm coax pitch, then slice 5 um discs and bond them to an access-transistor wafer. Coax pitch finer than pad pitch means each pad statistically lands on at least one coax.
why: Capacitor aspect ratio becomes free: a 5 um coax with a 20 nm glass wall gives ~3 fF without any high-AR etch (Fact 1, capital).

title: Spare-wafer remapping replaces known-good-die testing in wafer-on-wafer stacks
idea: Substitute die-level HBM stacking (TSV + microbump + known-good-die test) with wafer-on-wafer hybrid bonding of 9 full DRAM wafers, one a spare; every bank has a fuse-programmable vertical bypass in the base logic so a failed bank on tier k is remapped to the same footprint on the spare tier.
why: HBM TSV tax and 20-30% yield loss (fact 6): one bond step per wafer instead of per die; stack yield rises from ~0.92^8 = 51% to >85% for 12.5% area overhead.

title: Fluidic self-assembled memory-tile carpet on a glass panel
idea: IFR: 'memory chips place themselves.' Backward: make 100 um oxide-on-glass memory tiles with shape-coded keys and solder-coded faces, pour them as a slurry over a glass panel with matching wells, and let capillary and solder self-alignment seat millions in minutes, then wire them with panel redistribution layers.
why: Packaging and HBM tax (fact 6): tiny known-good tiles give ~99% effective yield; ~1e6 tiles/hour assembly without pick-and-place.

title: Turn lithography sideways: film thickness sets every critical dimension
idea: Move the critical dimension from lateral litho to vertical film thickness: gate length, channel thickness and capacitor dielectric are all LPCVD or sputter thicknesses with nm control, and the only litho is a 180-nm-pitch slot and hole pattern. That pattern is punched through eight 32-tier poly-Si decks (AR ~9 each), so a 0.065-um2 column over 256 tiers is ~0.00025 um2 per bit.
why: Litho-bound scaling and EUV capital (fact 4): ~3x denser than 6F2 at 12 nm using KrF/i-line-class tools and no EUV.

title: MEMS micromirror process fused with DRAM: nano-relay access switches
idea: Replace the access transistor with an electrostatic nano-cantilever relay built in a back-end sacrificial-gap MEMS flow like TI's Dallas DLP micromirror line; the open contact is a vacuum gap, so off-state leakage is essentially zero, and the relay sits above its capacitor in the same 4F2 footprint.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): no subthreshold or GIDL path, retention limited by dielectric leakage (minutes+), refresh almost gone; nm relays switch in ~10-50 ns, contact endurance (>10^15) is the risk.

title: Molecular monolayer doping replaces BF3/PF3 implants on 3D sidewalls
idea: Substitute beamline BF3/PF3/GeF4 implants (which cannot reach 100-tier hole sidewalls anyway) with monolayer doping: self-assembled allylboronic-acid-pinacol-ester or diethyl-vinylphosphonate monolayers coat every exposed Si sidewall, are capped with ALD oxide, and spike-annealed into ~5 nm conformal junctions on all tiers at once.
why: Dopes 3D DRAM lateral access transistors on every tier in one step (fact 2) without fluorinated dopant gases; abrupt shallow junctions cut GIDL, the leakage-tail driver (fact 3).
